hook.line: Get close to 21 without going over. The game’s name already appears in Spanish literature around 1600.
hook.say: Hit me with some blackjack history!

ch.say: It was played under the name “21”.
p: One early record is “veintiuna” (twenty-one) in a Cervantes short story published in 1613.
Via France’s “vingt-et-un” it reached America; a bonus paid for the ace of spades with a black jack is said to have given it the name “blackjack”.

tl: Reaches America and its gambling halls
Nevada legalises gambling; blackjack becomes a casino staple
Thorp’s book makes card counting famous

ch.say: An ace and a face card — blackjack!
p: The ace can be 1 or 11 — the all-rounder.
Twenty-one with your first two cards is a “blackjack”, usually paid at 3 to 2.

ch.say: Rules change a little from place to place.
cards: The British twenty-one; the dealer’s cards stay face down
Played with 48 cards — the tens removed
You may swap the second cards of two hands

ch.say: Some people studied how to beat the casino.
cards: A mathematician who used computers to show that tracking played cards can give the player the edge
Students who took on casinos with card counting — their story became a film

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Must draw another card — the dealer has no choice
Splitting a pair into two separate hands
Not in most places — but casinos may show you the door

p: One more card, or stop right here? That moment is the thrill.
